acceptance_criteria: AC-1 A backup job against the allowlisted device runs submit, poll, fetch, verify, delete in that order against a fake transport and records one artefact with its C7 manifest row; a job against any other device is refused with a reason naming the allowlist.

AC-2 A digest mismatch fails the run, deletes nothing on the device, and says which side differed; a never-terminal poll ends OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and deletes nothing; a failed delete records cleanup_failed and marks the endpoint ineligible.
AC-3 An unresolvable Check Point software version refuses the store with zero rows and a named failure; the deviation state is recorded against the previous artefact.

AC-4 The CLI retrieval decrypts to the operator's named path under the backup role with a reason, writes its audit row, and no HTTP route returns bytes, a path or a decrypt affordance (a test greps the service sources for a retrieval route and fails if one exists).

AC-5 Gate entries exist per literal, the migration seeds them SIGNED_OFF and the capability resolves executionEligible; eleven-module build, the named module tests, manifests, migration-audit-context, frontend tests, privacy gate and contract_authority_status all green.

baseline.what_exists: The configuration collection is the pattern to copy end to end: worker.configuration ConfigurationReadPlan (a closed literal set with its own equality test), ConfigurationCapabilityExecutor, ConfigurationJobExecutor (full C2 discipline: lease, fencing, heartbeat, terminal outcome, identity-mismatch handling), its gate entries documents and SIGNED_OFF gate_registry rows seeded by migration, its capability YAMLs with real steps and gate_reference, its end-to-end and worker-dies tests against a scripted fake DeviceTransport, its service routes and its screen. Merged since: the artefact store at the C7 shape -- ArtefactStore.open(deviceId, jobId, vendor, gzip) returns a handle whose metadata carries plaintext and ciphertext digests and byte counts, keyId and wrappedDataKey; ArtefactStore.retrieve(ref, wrappedDataKey, gzip) needs that wrapped key, so the master key alone decrypts nothing; BackupArtefactManifestRepository.record(manifest, actorFingerprint, actionId) writes the C7 manifest row; HostnameFingerprint.fromBase64Key(...).of(hostname) produces the HMAC fingerprint; the recovery volume is a worker-only PersistentVolumeClaim. Transport: SshExecTransport exposes exec over one session; check whether it exposes an SFTP/file-fetch call -- if it does not, add one to the transport port and the SSH adapter, streaming, with no path interpolation beyond the exact archive path the submit output named. ui2/cli holds the product's command line (the credential-* and local-identity-* commands are its existing shape). Migrations: use the next free number; a migration that writes a row to an audited table sets app.actor_fingerprint and app.action_id transaction-locally first (tests/test_migration_audit_context.py enforces it).

report.objective: Build the Check Point gateway backup: the backup_collect job kind and its capability, the gate entries and their SIGNED_OFF rows for the seven literals record 14H lifts, the submit-then-poll executor that 14H BK-5 requires (the frozen blocking-exec profile is wrong and is not carried), the SFTP fetch with a digest verified on both sides before any deletion, the pilot-device allowlist that refuses every other device, storage as a C7 backup artefact through the store that now carries per-artefact envelope encryption, deviation against the previous artefact, the audited command-line retrieval record 14I authorizes, and the backup view. output_contract: A Check Point gateway backup that runs on the pilot device, verifies before it deletes, stores an encrypted artefact with its manifest, and can be read back by the operator through the command line.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A class-1 device write with a state machine, a two-sided digest protocol, a gate set, an artefact manifest, a CLI retrieval and a screen, against two fresh frozen records.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every public type names the clause it implements (14H BK-n, 14I OR-n/DV-n, C7 section n, C2 section n).

Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite. Eleven Gradle subprojects. One additive migration at the next free number, setting the audit context before any row it writes.
No archive byte, no device path, no credential and no hostname reaches a log line, an exception message, an audit row beyond the columns the contract names, or any HTTP response.
The submit is issued at most once per job. Never derive an archive name from a listing, a pattern or a guess.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.

Commit early and often. SESSION_CLOSE names the gate entries count, the migration number, the capability id, the executor's state machine, the CLI command, the routes with status codes, and test counts before and after.
risks: Carrying the frozen blocking-exec profile instead of submit-then-poll, which records success before the archive exists.
Deleting on the device before the digest comparison, or deleting a name derived from a listing.
Retrying the submit and creating a second concurrent backup.
Letting the allowlist default to permissive.

in: Gate: docs/design/CP_BACKUP_COMMAND_GATE_ENTRIES.md in the DEVICE_FIRST_CONTACT_COMMAND_GATE_ENTRIES.md shape, one ten-field entry per literal of 14H section 5 (the clish -c wrapper is part of the literal), each stating its class honestly -- add backup local and delete backup are class 1 -- its timeout, its retry rule (the submit is never retried; the delete may be retried once), and the CONFIRM-ON-HARDWARE note on show diskspace and delete backup. The next free migration seeds the matching gate_registry rows SIGNED_OFF, and a resolver test proves the capability resolves executionEligible.

Capability and job: BackupCapabilityIds.CP_GAIA_BACKUP_LOCAL, its YAML with the real steps and gate references, the backup_collect job kind admitted only against an ENROLLED, non-disabled device that is ALSO in the pilot allowlist; admission of a device outside the allowlist is refused with a reason naming the allowlist, and a test proves both sides. The allowlist is configuration (an env-backed list of device ids, empty by default -- empty means every backup is refused).

Worker: BackupReadPlan (the closed literal set, tested equal to 14H section 5) and BackupJobExecutor with the C2 discipline of ConfigurationJobExecutor, performing: resolve the distinct backup credential (BK-11, failing closed with a named reason before contact), read free space and compare against the configurable heuristic threshold (BK-6), submit the backup, parse the archive name from the submit output ONLY, poll the status command on a fixed interval until terminal or the run deadline (BK-5), fetch the archive over SFTP streaming straight into the artefact store, compute a digest on the device and compare it with the digest of the received bytes (BK-3) -- on mismatch fail, leave the device copy, and say so -- then delete the exact archive name and record cleanup_failed as a failure marking the endpoint ineligible if the delete fails. A poll that never terminates ends OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and deletes nothing. A vendor refusal (a snapshot in progress, an open management client) is reported as the failure reason, never retried.

Storage and deviation: the archive is stored through the artefact store with artefact class backup, and a C7 manifest row is written with both digests, byte counts, the hostname fingerprint, the software version (BK-16/C7 section 3.3: an unresolvable Check Point software version refuses the store with zero rows and a named failure), the validation level reached and the wrapped data key. DV-1: the run records unchanged / changed / first against the previous backup artefact of the same device by plaintext digest; DV-3: for the opaque archive the deviation is digest-level only and the run says so.

Operator retrieval (14I OR-1..OR-5): a command in ui2/cli that takes an artefact id, an output path, and a reason of at least eight characters, checks role:backup_admin, decrypts through the store to that path and nowhere else, writes a typed audit row with the actor, the artefact id, the reason and the destination, and prints one warning that the file contains secret-bearing lines. No HTTP route of any kind returns bytes, a path or a decrypt affordance.

Service and screen: POST /devices/{id}/backup/collect (202 {job_id}; 409 with a named reason when the device is outside the allowlist or the credential is missing), GET /devices/{id}/backups (the manifest rows for that device: when, size, digest prefix, validation level, deviation state -- never a path, never bytes), GET /backups for the fleet view; the Operations or Configuration screen gains a backup panel showing those rows and a Back up now action, with the reason field the role requires. No download affordance anywhere.
